question: On 18 August 2026, Markus Lammert, the Commission spokesperson for home affairs, made concerning statements encouraging the expulsion of people who had arrived in Ceuta, including unaccompanied minors and persons in need of international protection, who are entitled to legal safeguards regardless of their migration status.

It is particularly serious that the Commission would encourage a Member State to act in breach of international and European law, while also failing to ensure individual assessments, access to the asylum procedure, the principle of non-refoulement and the best interests of the child, as well as obligations arising from EU fundamental rights and under international conventions. In this context: 1.
What is the Commission’s priority in responding to the crisis in Ceuta: expulsions or ensuring humanitarian assistance, fundamental rights protection and effective access to international protection?

Under what legal framework did Mr Lammert propose the expulsion of minors and persons who have expressed their intention to apply for international protection, and does the Commission consider his statements as being compatible with this legal framework?

Given that Ceuta is an external border of the EU, will the Commission provide extraordinary financial assistance to Spain and investigate Morocco’s possible role in this crisis, and if geopolitical interference in EU and Spanish sovereignty is established, what measures will it take against the countries responsible?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.11.2026) The position of the Commission in relation to the situation in Ceuta has been clear and consistent from the outset: those, who arrived illegally and are not allowed to stay on any of the grounds foreseen by EU law or the Spanish national law, must return.

This is the responsibility of the Spanish national authorities acting in compliance with the applicable legal framework, and in respect of fundamental rights, including the principle of nonrefoulement. In this process, and in line with the applicable EU law, those, seeking international protection, must be given access to the asylum procedure.

For actions relating to minors, the child’s best interests must be a primary consideration. It is in this context that, during the midday briefing of 18 August 2026, the Commission spokesperson for internal affairs referred to the relevant legal basis (the Return Directive1 and soon the EU Return Regulation2).

The Commission has offered support to Spain from the very first day to address the situation in Ceuta, both in the form of financial and operational assistance. As regards EU emergency funding to address the situation in Ceuta, a total of EUR 114.7 million were made available to Spain (EUR 82.

7 million under the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund and EUR 32 million under the Border Management and Visa Instrument). The Commission is also coordinating and facilitating the mobilisation of support from the EU agencies, notably the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, the EU Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation and the EU Agency for Asylum.

This further strengthens the assistance available to the Spanish authorities to manage the situation on the ground3. It is the competence and responsibility of Spanish authorities to establish the facts and determine any responsibility.
1 Directive 2008/115/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on common
standards and procedures in Member States for returning illegally staying third-country nationals (OJ L 348, 24.12.2008: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2008/115/oj/eng).

2 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a common system for the return of third-country nationals staying illegally in the Union and repealing Directive 2008/115/EC of the European Parliament and the Council, Council Directive 2001/40/EC and Council Decision 2004/191/EC, COM/2025/101 final: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025PC0101.
The publication of the final text that was adopted by the co-legislators in the Official Journal is forthcoming. 3 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_26_1799.
